items.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024
items.q: I met Jimmy in New York... I was doing a lot of work... we're in the studio playing

ctx.x: Nope. No it was commercial, mediocre, and people tell me, they say, “Oh you’re on that, that’s a classic, that’s a classic.” Well no, no, Charlie Parker on “Jazz at Massey Hall” that’s a classic. Art Tatum playing “Tenderly,” that’s a classic. You know? Billie Holiday singing anything you know, those are classics.
Okay. Before we leave that I just looked to my left here and amongst the people I see you’ve played with if this is correct is a drummer named Jimmy Wormworth.

Well yeah, I met Jimmy in New York through Mike Kanan which actually came through Jorge Rossi. I had a short period, five or six years, where I was going back to New York about every six weeks I would go for ten days. I had a room I rented from Mike Kanan and his wife Stephanie. And I was doing a lot of work and I began to turn down some work because all I wanted to do was play with those guys, you know, and Mike had a studio and so I was playing — I would get to New York about 6 or 7 the plane would come in at…
